title: ACME - incident timeline & debug scratchpad (draft)
body:
Quick notes / scratchpad for ACME incident (draft internal timeline + comms).

Overview:
- Customer: ACME Corp (high-volume account on Dedicated pool).
- Symptom: Starting ~2026-02-27T09:15Z customers reported elevated 502/503 errors and slow token generation (~3-4x latency).
- Impact: ~20% of requests for ACME app failed with HTTP 502/503 intermittently; others experienced high tail latency.
- Current status: Mitigations applied (routing to reserve pool + temporary rate-limits). Errors reduced but root cause not confirmed.

Timeline (raw notes):
- 2026-02-27 09:12 UTC: First alert from monitoring (error rate spike) - page to oncall (Devon).
- 2026-02-27 09:16 UTC: CS (me) got ping from ACME SRE (they reported errors in prod).
- 2026-02-27 09:18 UTC: Devon started collection: increased logging, enabled debug-level for redwood-serving for ACME tenant.
- 2026-02-27 09:25 UTC: Observed repeated "model not ready" / "gateway: upstream read timeout" in nginx logs for dedicated pool nodes.
- 2026-02-27 09:30 UTC: Applied temporary routing to reserve pool for high-priority ACME routes. Error rate dropped from ~18% -> ~4% within 5m.
- 2026-02-27 10:05 UTC: Started deeper investigation into runner node logs and GPU metrics.
- 2026-02-27 10:18 UTC: Noticed memory pressure on 2/6 GPUs on pool-az1-node-5 (cuda mem used ~98%).
- 2026-02-27 10:35 UTC: Restarted runner pod on pool-az1-node-5; error rate normalized for that node but others showed transient spikes.
- 2026-02-27 11:00 UTC: Eng requesting dumps and longer-term traces; requested support from infra for kernel OOM logs.

Commands we ran (copied from shell):
- kubectl -n redwood get pods -l tenant=acme -o wide
  -> runner-acme-6d8f5  Running   3/3   10.2.1.45   pool-az1-node-5

- kubectl -n redwood logs runner-acme-6d8f5 -c server --since=30m | tail -n 200\  
  -> [2026-02-27T09:24:56Z] WARN  redwood.server  gateway: upstream read timeout (client_id=acme-web)
  -> [2026-02-27T09:25:03Z] ERROR redwood.model  model-loader: failed to allocate KV cache (requested 2.1GB, available 80MB)

- redwoodctl get-sessions --tenant acme --since 2026-02-27T08:00Z --status error
  -> session ids: s_1234, s_1235, s_1236 (burst around 09:15-09:35)

- curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <ACME-API-KEY>" -d '{"model":"gpt-neoX-20b","input":"hello"}' https://dedicated-us1.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
  -> * Connected to dedicated-us1.api.redwood.ai
  -> < HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
  -> {"error":"upstream response timeout"}

Relevant log snippets (copied):
- "ERROR model-runner: RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.5 GiB (GPU 0; 31.75 GiB total capacity; 30.9 GiB already allocated)
   at /opt/conda/lib/python3.10/site-packages/torch/cuda/memory.py:...
   during model.forward()
"

- "WARN kv-cache: eviction triggered. hit_rate drop from 0.92 -> 0.34 in 3m for tenant acme"

- "INFO routing: failover invoked for route /v1/generate (tenant acme) -> fallback to reserve-pool-1"

Hypotheses (ordered by my confidence):
1) Memory pressure on specific GPUs due to sudden workload pattern (longer context lengths causing high KV cache retention) leading to OOMs and model reloads -> triggering upstream timeouts.
2) A regression in model-loader memory accounting after last infra change leading to under-reporting of reserved memory and overcommitting GPUs.
3) Network/backpressure between gateway and runner (less likely given GPU mem warnings).
4) KV cache corruption leading to repeated cache misses and load storms (low confidence but correlates with kv-cache eviction warnings).

Immediate next steps I pushed for:
- (Done) Route critical ACME traffic to reserve pool and apply temporary rate limits to reduce burst.
- (In progress) Collect full dmesg + nvidia-smi --query output for the affected nodes (asked infra).
- (In progress) Dump model-loader allocations and track sequence-length distribution for ACME requests (Eng - Jamie).
- (Planned) Reproduce with loadtest simulating ACME request patterns (long contexts + many small parallel requests).
- (Planned) If model-loader regression suspected, bisect infra change from 2026-02-20 -> 2026-02-26 (Devon).

Notes for postmortem (things to capture):
- exact sequence length distribution and average tokens per request for ACME in the incident window.
- which nodes had repeated OOMs and runner restarts and timestamps.
- any infra changes/rollouts overlapping (kernel, cuda, driver, libtorch, redwood-serving image).
- whether fallback/reserve pool paid down the queue or if requests were dropped.

Draft internal update (copy / paste, tweak before sending to eng/cs leads):
Subject: ACME incident 2026-02-27 - elevated 502s / GPU memory pressure (draft)
Hi team,

TL;DR: ACME experienced increased 502/503 errors between ~09:12-10:30 UTC due to GPU memory pressure in their Dedicated pool causing OOMs and upstream timeouts. Temporary mitigation was to route ACME traffic to reserve pool and apply rate-limits; error rate dropped to ~4%. Engineering investigating model-loader memory accounting and request pattern (long contexts).

What happened:
- Monitoring alerted at 09:12 UTC for ACME; logs showed repeated "upstream read timeout" and CUDA OOM errors on pool-az1-node-5 and one other node.
- We applied routing to reserve pool at 09:30 UTC which reduced customer impact.

Actions taken so far:
- Scoped to ACME tenant, enabled debug logs, collected runner logs.
- Restarted affected runner pod(s) and confirmed immediate improvement on those nodes.
- Eng collecting dmesg and nvidia-smi outputs and will attempt to reproduce.

Requested next steps from Eng:
- Confirm whether a recent infra change impacted model-loader memory accounting (candidate changes 2026-02-20 -> 2026-02-26).
- Produce reproduction of ACME workload (seq-length distribution) in staging and test model-loader behavior.
- If regression found, prepare hotfix to avoid overcommit (patch + canary).

Customer-facing note (short draft to run by legal/CS):
We experienced an elevated error rate affecting ACME on 2026-02-27 due to memory pressure in the Dedicated inference pool. We routed traffic to a reserve pool and applied temporary limits to minimize impact. We are actively investigating the root cause and will share findings and remediation steps by EOD.

Open questions / things I still need to check:
- Are there any overlapping infra rollouts in pool-az1 during the window? (kernel/drivers/libtorch/cuda)
- Is ACME sending longer contexts suddenly (new feature?) or did their traffic pattern change? (CS to confirm with ACME SRE).
- Are there other tenants showing similar kv-cache eviction patterns? (Jamie to query metrics).

Raw debugging checklist (for follow-up runbook):
- collect /var/log/kern.log and dmesg for nodes with restarts
- nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.total,memory.used,utilization.gpu --format=csv -l 1 for 10m through window
- redwoodctl dump-allocations --node pool-az1-node-5 --since 2026-02-27T08:00Z > /tmp/allocs-node5.log
- capture full request payload samples (sanitized) for long contexts

Personal notes: keep comms short and precise. we want to avoid speculative blame to infra in the user-facing note.

-- Ava

(End of draft)
